messages:
maria: FYI customer (acme-inc) hit a mid-stream 429 during SSE; their client retried and they saw token accounting that looks like a double charge. asking for an audit.

alex: can you paste the exact client repro + headers? need to check session id + resume token behavior.

maria: steps from customer: 1) start SSE stream to /v1/stream with Authorization: Bearer <key> 2) after ~12s connection gets HTTP 429 mid-event 3) client reconnects with same key + `x-resume-session: s-abc123` 4) server returns 200 and continues, but billing shows both partial charge and resumed charge counted. they attached server->ledger dump.

alex: pinging @devon and @ops-jen for infra + billing correlation. can we pull proxy logs for connection and resume handoff?

devon: got the logs for session s-abc123. I see upstream SSE chunk stopped with `HTTP/1.1 429` at 2025-10-12T14:33:21Z then a new connection at 2025-10-12T14:33:23Z with header `x-resume-session: s-abc123`.

ops-jen: interestingly the resume path returned a `resume-ttl-claim` success: "claimed-ttl=300" and we emitted an event `resume:claimed` in trace. but billing ledger shows two separate charge records: `charge_id=chg-111 tokens=94 status=posted` (from first connection) and `charge_id=chg-112 tokens=86 status=posted` (from resumed).

alex: do we have any server-side dedupe on resume? i thought resume should only forward uncharged tokens. @devon?

devon: current logic: when resume token is valid we reattach KV cache and continue; we call `finalize_charge` for the previous stream only when server emits `stream_end`. If 429 happens mid-stream we set previous connection to `errored` and run `finalize_charge` immediately which posts the partial charge. resume then starts a new charge window and posts another. so double post is expected under current model.

maria: customer expectation was resume should continue same billing window when reconnect within TTL. they hit a long-ish response where 429 was transient and client retried immediately.

ops-jen: the mismatch rule: we attempted to prevent double billing by marking `finalize_after_grace=5s` but 429 path forces immediate finalize. logs:```
[2025-10-12T14:33:21Z] session=s-abc123 event=recv status=429 conn=12
[2025-10-12T14:33:21Z] session=s-abc123 action=finalize_charge charge_id=chg-111 tokens=94 reason=rate_limit
[2025-10-12T14:33:23Z] session=s-abc123 event=conn_new resume_header=true conn=13
[2025-10-12T14:33:23Z] session=s-abc123 action=create_charge charge_id=chg-112 tokens=0 status=pending
[2025-10-12T14:33:27Z] session=s-abc123 action=post_tokens charge_id=chg-112 tokens=86
```

alex: OK. sounds like a product expectation gap. what are mitigation options? immediate ideas: 1) treat 429 as transient and keep previous charge window open for resume TTL instead of finalizing; 2) on resume, detect recent `finalize` due to rate_limit within TTL and attempt to merge charges server-side + emit a single invoice adjustment; 3) provide client guidance: exponential backoff and use `x-resume-claim` semantics to avoid immediate new charge.

maria: customer asked for timeline — they want credits if double-charged. can billing team confirm whether we can merge or issue refund? @billing-bot any quick take?

billing-bot: auto-check: found both posted charges chg-111 and chg-112 to account acme-inc during invoice cycle 2025-10. Policy: we can issue a one-off credit if duplicate root cause is platform bug. need eng confirm root cause + a short incident note.

devon: root cause = server finalizes on 429; that's by design but not documented for resume semantics. I'll open an engineering task: make 429 path set `finalize_after_grace=ttl` and only finalize after grace unless explicit `stream_end`. short-term we can add a ledger reconciliation job to merge near-duplicate charges where session id and timestamps match pattern.

ops-jen: I can prototype merging logic on billing side. low-risk path: detect two charges within 10s for same session id and mark one as adjustment. will need audit trail.

maria: for immediate customer-facing steps: 1) offer one-off credit for duplicated tokens (ask billing to prepare credit) 2) recommend client retry policy: backoff 250ms -> 1s -> 2s and include `x-resume-session` header 3) notify them we'll follow up with timeline for platform fix.

alex: THanks. I'll file a support follow-up and request credits. Maria, can you draft the message? keep it short.

maria: draft: "We reproduced the billing behavior — server finalizes partial charge when a 429 occurs mid-stream and a reconnect then starts a new charge. We're issuing a one-time credit for the duplicate tokens and engineering will modify resume/429 handling to avoid this in future. ETA 2 weeks for a fix. Apologies."

alex: looks good. @devon please create an ENG ticket linking logs + proposed fix. include test plan to repro with synthetic client that forces mid-stream 429 and immediate resume.

devon: will do. Creating ENG-1153: "sse: preserve billing window across transient 429/resume within TTL" and attaching repro script.

ops-jen: putting a temporary reconciliation job in place today to detect duplicates; I'll coordinate with billing for credits.

maria: closing loop: customer accepts provisional credit while we patch. thanks team :thumbsup:

support-bot: incident-note created: ENG-1153 linked, billing-credit pending, customer notified."
